To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the x-ray units can be used to produce x-ray images of aircraft and the neutron unit can be used to inspect aircraft for corrosion.
a 4 MeV, 1.2 kW, x-ray source has been developed which can produce 10-20 W of x-rays with 1 mm focal spot at a rate of 10 Hz.
a high power, 9.3GHz, coaxial magnetron is capable of producing a 1.3MW average power output at 2.2kW input, with 50% duty factor, at a 1% duty factor the power output is 1.5 MW.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication of the RF sources, accelerating waveguides, and power supplies.
the development of high-power, high-frequency microwave components for use in the generation of x-rays and fast neutrons.
the development of x-ray and neutron sources for nondestructive evaluation of materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 6 MeV system, as presently designed, is the most practical and cost-effective means of providing a portable neutron source of the type required.
the x-band linear accelerator is a very practical and efficient device which is capable of providing high power, high energy, high quality beams of x-rays or neutras.
the x-band accelerators are very attractive for use in nondestructive testing because of the high power, high efficiency and light weight of the magnetron and the accelerator system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 9.3 Ghz frequency is not the ideal frequency for this application.
we were successful in developing three light-weight x-ray and neutron generators that are highly portable.
the x-ray and neutron sources developed have proven to be extremely portable and have demonstrated excellent performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the traveling wave structure in the 4 MeV system is not necessary for the generation of x-rays, and that the standing wave guide is an excellent structure for the production of x-rays or neutrays at the 6 MeV level.
the x-ray unit has been built, tested, and delivered to the user and that the neutron unit has been designed and is being fabricated.
the use of a high power RF magnetron as an RF power source is a viable option for the development of a portable, high power, linear electron accelerator.
